links.outcome: Whether benchmark accuracy predicts clinical reliability under sycophancy pressure
links.effect: Reasoning-optimized Thinking models show high vanilla accuracy but rationalize incorrect user suggestions under authoritative pressure; benchmark performance is not a proxy for clinical reliability.
links.quote: Our results across frontier models suggest that benchmark performance is not a proxy for clinical reliability, and that simplified reasoning structures may offer superior robustness against expert-driven sycophancy.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of LLM sycophancy (alignment bias under user pressure) on medical multiple-choice question answering benchmarks.
